title.zh: 卷四十一 列傳第十一 魏舒 李憙 劉寔 高光
title.en: Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang
title.raw: 卷四十一 列傳第十一 魏舒 李憙 劉寔 高光 Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang

sentences.zh: 魏舒，字陽元，任城樊人也。

translations.literal: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Fan in Rencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為外家寧氏所養。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was reared by his maternal kin, the Ning clan.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father while still young and was brought up by his mother's people, the Nings.

sentences.zh: 寧氏起宅，相宅者云：「當出貴甥。

translations.literal: The Ning family built a house, and a geomancer of the site said, "A noble nephew will come forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nings raised a new house, a geomancer told them, "This site will produce a distinguished nephew."

sentences.zh: 」外祖母以魏氏甥小而慧，意謂應之。

translations.literal: " His maternal grandmother, because the Wei nephew was small yet clever, in her mind thought it referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandmother, seeing that the Wei boy was young but bright, assumed the omen pointed to him.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「當為外氏成此宅相。

translations.literal: Shu said, "I shall for the maternal clan complete this houselot omen.
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "It falls to me to fulfill that houselot prophecy for our mother's family."

sentences.zh: 」久乃別居。

translations.literal: " After a long time then he lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: Only after many years did he move out and keep a separate household.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi two cun in height, his bearing fine and grand, he drank more than a shi of wine, yet was slow, dull, plain, and was not esteemed by townsmen and kin.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi and two cun tall, carried himself with striking presence, and could put away more than a shi of wine, yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors and relatives thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！

translations.literal: His father's cousin, Ning Heng, Personnel Ministry gentleman, had fame in the age, also did not know him, made him guard the water trip-hammer, and often sighed, saying, "Shu can suffice as chief of several hundred households — my wishes are fulfilled!
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Ning Heng, a Personnel Ministry officer celebrated in their day, never recognized his gifts either and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, "If Shu can serve as headman over a few hundred households, I shall ask nothing more!"

sentences.zh: 」舒亦不以介意。

translations.literal: " Shu also did not on that account take it to mind.
translations.idiomatic: Shu did not resent him for it.

sentences.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。

translations.literal: He did not cultivate ordinary men's scruples, did not do bright-harsh matters, always wished to accommodate talent and lengthen things, and to the end did not display people's shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: He scorned petty convention and avoided ostentatious moralism, preferring always to nurture others' strengths and never to expose their faults.

sentences.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。

translations.literal: By nature he loved riding and shooting, and wore leather garments.
translations.idiomatic: He loved riding and archery and habitually dressed in leather hunting clothes.

sentences.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。

translations.literal: He entered mountains and marshes and took fishing and hunting as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He roamed hills and wetlands and made fishing and hunting his chief pastime.

sentences.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。

translations.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu, "You in the end will become a pillar minister, yet now are not able to cause wife and children to escape cold and hunger; I shall help you arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi of Taiyuan alone told him, "You are destined for the highest councils of state, yet you cannot yet keep your wife and children from want; let me help you set them up."

sentences.zh: 」常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。

translations.literal: " He regularly relieved their want; Shu accepted and did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Wang regularly supplied what the household lacked, and Shu accepted without demur.

sentences.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？

translations.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host's wife gave birth in the night; presently they heard the sound of horses and chariots, mutually asking, "Male or female?
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Yewang, while his host's wife labored in the night, voices like chariots and horses suddenly sounded outside, asking, "Boy or girl?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。

translations.literal: " It was said, "Male; write it; at fifteen he will die by weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "A son. Record it—he will die by the sword at fifteen."

sentences.zh: 」復問：「寢者為誰？

translations.literal: " Again they asked, "Who is the one sleeping?
translations.idiomatic: Then they asked, "Who lies abed here?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「魏公舒。

translations.literal: " It was said, "Lord Wei Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "Wei Shu of Wei commandery."

sentences.zh: 」後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。

translations.literal: " After fifteen years he went to the host, asked where the born child was, and it was said, "Because trimming mulberry he was wounded by an axe and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later he looked up the host and asked after that child; the man said, "He died when an axe slipped as he was pruning mulberry."

sentences.zh: 」舒自知當為公矣。

translations.literal: " Shu himself knew he would become a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Shu understood then that he was fated to rise to the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，郡上計掾察孝廉。

translations.literal: His years being more than forty, the commandery chief clerk on the accounts mission nominated him Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty he went up with the commandery accounts as clerk and was nominated Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 宗党以舒無學業，勸令不就，可以為高耳。

translations.literal: Clan and party, because Shu had no scholarly learning, urged him to order not to take office, and thereby could be lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen, noting that he had never mastered the classics, urged him to stay home so he might pass for a lofty recluse.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「若試而不中，其負在我，安可虛竊不就之高以為己榮乎！

translations.literal: Shu said, "If I try and do not pass, the burden is on me; how can I vainly steal the height of not going and make it my glory!
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "If I sit the examination and fail, the fault is mine; I will not borrow the empty fame of refusing office and call it honor."

sentences.zh: 」於是自課。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he self-set lessons.
translations.idiomatic: So he drew up a strict course of study for himself.

sentences.zh: 百日習一經，因而對策升第。

translations.literal: In a hundred days he studied one classic, and thereby in policy examination rose in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred days he mastered one classic, passed the policy examination, and took top placement.

sentences.zh: 除澠池長，遷浚儀令，入為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief of Mianchi, transferred to magistrate of Junyi, entered as Secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief of Mianchi, promoted to magistrate of Junyi, and then called to the capital as a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時欲沙汰郎官。

translations.literal: At the time they wished to sift and wash out Secretariat gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The court then meant to weed out the gentlemen of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 非其才者罷之。

translations.literal: Those not of their talent were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who lacked the requisite ability would be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「吾即其人也。

translations.literal: Shu said, "I am precisely that person.
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "I am one of those you mean to remove."

sentences.zh: 」襆被而出。

translations.literal: " Bundling bedding he went out.
translations.idiomatic: He bundled his bedding and walked out.

sentences.zh: 同僚素無清論者咸有愧色，談者稱之。

translations.literal: Colleagues who plain had no pure discussion all had ashamed color; those who talked praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow officers who had never enjoyed a reputation for integrity colored with shame; men who discussed the affair praised him.

sentences.zh: 累遷後將軍鐘毓長史，毓每與參佐射，舒常為畫籌而已。

translations.literal: By accumulated transfers he became chief clerk to Rear General Zhong Yu; whenever Yu with staff assistants shot, Shu always merely made the tally marks.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted step by step, he became chief clerk to Rear General Zhong Yu; whenever Yu held an archery contest with his staff, Shu merely kept score and never shot.

sentences.zh: 後遇朋人不足，以舒滿數。

translations.literal: Later encountering companion men insufficient, they used Shu to fill the number.
translations.idiomatic: Once there were not enough archers to make up the teams, they added Shu to complete the roster.

sentences.zh: 毓初不知其善射。

translations.literal: Yu at first did not know his being good at shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu had not known he could shoot.

sentences.zh: 舒容范閒雅，發無不中，舉坐愕然。

translations.literal: Shu's bearing was model, leisurely and elegant; loosing, there was none that did not hit; the whole seated company was stunned.
translations.idiomatic: Shu stepped forward with unhurried grace; every arrow found its mark, and the whole company sat speechless.

sentences.zh: 莫有敵者。

translations.literal: There was none who matched him.
translations.idiomatic: No one there could match him.

sentences.zh: 毓歎而謝曰：「吾之不足以盡卿才，有如此射矣，豈一事哉！

translations.literal: Yu sighed and apologized, saying, "My insufficiency to exhaust your talent is like this shooting — is it one matter only!
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu sighed and apologized: "If I have failed until now to use your abilities, today's archery shows why—this is hardly the only thing you excel at!"

sentences.zh: 」轉相國參軍，封劇陽子。

translations.literal: " He was transferred aide in the state ministry and enfeoffed as viscount of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as an aide in the chancellor's headquarters and enfeoffed as viscount of Ji.

sentences.zh: 府朝碎務，未嘗見是非；

translations.literal: For the bureau court fragment affairs, he never showed right and wrong;
translations.idiomatic: In the routine paperwork of the bureau he never picked petty quarrels;

sentences.zh: 至於廢興大事，眾人莫能斷者，舒徐為籌之，多出眾議之表。

translations.literal: as for great matters of abolishing and raising, where the crowd of men could not decide, Shu slowly for them planned, often going out beyond the crowd of proposals' surface.
translations.idiomatic: yet on great questions of state where the assembly could not agree, he would think them through quietly and often surpassed anything the others had proposed.

sentences.zh: 文帝深器重之，每朝會坐罷，目送之曰：「魏舒堂堂，人之領袖也。

translations.literal: Prince Wen deeply valued him; each court assembly when seating finished, watching him leave with eyes said, "Wei Shu is imposing; he is men's collar and sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen of Jin thought the world of him; after each court session he would watch Shu withdraw and murmur, "Wei Shu carries himself like a true leader among men."

sentences.zh: 」遷宜陽、滎陽二郡太守，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: " He was transferred governor of the two commanderies Yiyang and Xingyang, and had very much reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Yiyang and Xingyang, where he earned wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 徵拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him and named him Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，在州三年，以簡惠稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province; being in the province three years, by simplicity and kindness he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of Ji Province and, across three years there, won praise for a light touch and humane government.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: He entered as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝以舒清素，特賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Shu was pure and plain, specially bestowed one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, knowing how spare and honest Shu lived, sent him a special gift of a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，以公事當免官，詔以贖論。

translations.literal: He was transferred Minister of the Secretariat; because of public affairs he ought to have been removed from office; an edict ordered discussion by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to minister of the Secretariat, he faced dismissal over an official matter, but an edict allowed him to commute the penalty with a fine.

sentences.zh: 舒三娶妻皆亡，是歲自表乞假還本郡葬妻，詔賜葬地一頃，錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Shu three times took wives and all died; that year he self-memorialized begging leave to return to the native commandery to bury his wife; an edict bestowed one qing burial land and five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Three wives in succession had died; that year he asked leave to return to his home commandery for the burial, and the throne granted him one qing of cemetery land and five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 太康初，拜右僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang he was appointed Right Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taikang era he was appointed right vice-director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 舒與衛瓘、山濤、張華等以六合混一，宜用古典封禪東嶽，前後累陳其事，帝謙讓不許。

translations.literal: Shu together with Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others, because the six directions were mixed in one, held it proper to use classical rites to feng and shan at the eastern marchmount; before and after repeatedly they presented this matter; the emperor modestly yielded and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Shu joined Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others in arguing that, with the realm reunited, the court ought to revive the classical Feng and Shan sacrifices on Mount Tai; they pressed the point in memorial after memorial, but the emperor modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 以舒為左僕射，領吏部。

translations.literal: They appointed Shu Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, concurrently heading the Personnel Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was named left vice-director of the Masters of Writing and placed in charge of the Personnel Ministry.

sentences.zh: 舒上言：「今選六宮，聘以玉帛，而舊使禦府丞奉聘，宣成嘉禮，贄重使輕。

translations.literal: Shu submitted words: "Now in selecting the six palaces betrothal uses jade and silk, yet the old practice sends the Palace Storehouse deputy to carry betrothal, proclaiming and completing the fine rite, while the gifts are heavy and the envoy light.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized: "Selection for the six palaces still relies on jade and silk betrothal gifts, yet we continue to send the deputy superintendent of the palace storehouse as envoy—the treasure is weighty while the messenger is slight."

sentences.zh: 以為拜三夫人宜使卿，九嬪使五官中郎將，美人、良人使謁者，於典制為弘。

translations.literal: I hold that for investing the three great consorts it is proper to use ministers, for the nine concubines to use Gentlemen of the Household for All Purposes, for beauties and chosen ladies to use heralds — toward canonical regulation this is magnified.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that investiture of the three senior consorts be entrusted to ministers, the nine imperial concubines to gentlemen of the household for all purposes, and the lower ranks of palace ladies to court heralds—so the ritual weight matches the statutes."

sentences.zh: 」有詔詳之，眾議異同，遂寢。

translations.literal: " There was an edict to deliberate it in detail; the crowd's discussions differed in agreement, and therefore it slept.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a full discussion, but opinions clashed and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 加右光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was added Grand Master of the Right with parity of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional titles of grand master of the right and privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 及山濤薨，以舒領司徒，有頃即真。

translations.literal: When Shan Tao died, they ordered Shu to act as Minister of Education; after a little while he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan Tao died, Shu was ordered to oversee the ministry of education and soon received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 舒有威重德望，祿賜散之九族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Shu had awesome weight and virtuous repute; stipends and gifts he scattered among the nine kinships; the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Shu combined moral authority with high prestige; stipends and gifts he shared across his entire kindred, leaving nothing hoarded at home.

sentences.zh: 陳留周震累為諸府所辟，辟書既下，公輒喪亡，僉號震為殺公掾，莫有辟者。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu repeatedly was summoned by various bureaus; once the summons letter had descended, the grandee always died; all called Zhen the adjutant who kills lords, and there was none who summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu had been summoned again and again, yet each time the appointment was issued his patron died; people called him the adjutant who killed his superiors, and no one would hire him.

sentences.zh: 舒乃命之，而竟無患，識者以此稱其達命。

translations.literal: Shu then ordered him, and in the end there was no calamity; those who knew praised him on this account as comprehending destiny.
translations.idiomatic: Shu summoned him nonetheless, and no misfortune followed; observers praised this as proof of Shu's grasp of fate.

sentences.zh: 以年老，每稱疾遜位。

translations.literal: Because of old age, he repeatedly claimed illness to yield position.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he often pleaded illness in order to resign.

sentences.zh: 中復暫起，署兗州中正，尋又稱疾。

translations.literal: In the middle again he briefly rose, was appointed middle appraiser of Yan Province, and presently again claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly returned to office as middle appraiser for Yan Province, then again pleaded sickness.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞郤詵與舒書曰：「公久疾小差，視事是也，唯上所念。

translations.literal: Xi Shen, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, wrote Shu a letter, saying, "You have long been ill and slightly improved; attending to affairs is right — it is what those above think of.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen, left assistant in the Secretariat, wrote: "You have been ill a long time but are a little better; resuming duty is what the throne expects."

sentences.zh: 何竟起訖還臥，曲身回法，甚失具瞻之望。

translations.literal: Why altogether rise and finish and return to bed, bending the body and twisting the law — greatly losing the expectation of being looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: Why rise only to go straight back to bed, bending every rule? You disappoint the court that looks to you for guidance."

sentences.zh: 公少立巍巍，一旦棄之，可不惜哉！

translations.literal: You from youth established towering height; in one morning to cast it — can it not be pitied!
translations.idiomatic: You built a towering reputation in youth—to throw it away now would be a bitter waste!"

sentences.zh: 」舒稱疾如初。

translations.literal: " Shu claimed illness as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pleaded illness as stubbornly as before.

sentences.zh: 後以災異遜位，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Later because of disasters and anomalies he yielded position; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Later he cited portents and offered to retire, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 後因正旦朝罷還第，表送章綬。

translations.literal: Later because on New Year's dawn court finished he returned to mansion and memorialized sending seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: Then, after New Year's court, he went home and submitted his seals and ribbons of office.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔敦勉。

translations.literal: The emperor by hand edict earnestly urged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a personal edict urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 而舒執意彌固，乃下詔曰：「司徒、劇陽子舒，體道弘粹，思量經遠，忠肅居正，在公盡規。

translations.literal: Yet Shu held his intent more firm; then an edict was issued, saying, "Minister of Education, Viscount of Ji, Shu embodies the Way in broad purity, thought and measure reach far, loyal and reverent he holds to the straight, in public he exhausts regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Shu only dug in harder, so the throne issued an edict: "Minister of Education and Viscount of Ji, Wei Shu, embodies the Way in its pure breadth; his plans look far ahead; he is loyal, grave, and upright, and in office he has never stinted honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 入管銓衡，官人允敘；

translations.literal: Within he managed the balance of appointments, ranking officials in suitable order;
translations.idiomatic: Within the ministry he balanced appointments so that every post went to a fitting man;

sentences.zh: 出贊袞職，敷弘五教。

translations.literal: without he assisted the ducal robe office, spread and enlarged the five teachings.
translations.idiomatic: without he aided the highest councils and spread the five teachings of moral order.

sentences.zh: 惠訓播流，德聲茂著，可謂朝之俊乂者也。

translations.literal: Kind instruction spreads and flows; virtuous fame flourishes bright — he may be called the court's outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: His gentle instruction has spread everywhere and his virtuous name shines bright—he is truly one of the great pillars of the court."

sentences.zh: 而屢執沖讓，辭旨懇誠，申覽反覆，省用憮然。

translations.literal: Yet repeatedly he presses modest yielding; his words' intent is earnest and sincere; extending and viewing back and forth, examining it I am sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he presses his modest resignations again and again, and each memorial is so earnest that, reading them back and forth, I cannot but grieve."

sentences.zh: 蓋成人之美，先典所與，難違至情。

translations.literal: For crowning others' excellence is what former canons grant; it is hard to reject utmost feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient canons praise those who crown another man's excellence, and I cannot lightly set aside such heartfelt devotion."

sentences.zh: 今聽其所執，以劇陽子就第，位同三司，祿賜如前。

translations.literal: Now I listen to what he insists on: as Viscount of Ji he goes to mansion, rank equal to Three Dukes, stipends and gifts as before.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore grant what he asks: he may retire to his mansion as viscount of Ji with rank equal to the Three Dukes and stipends as before."

sentences.zh: 几杖不朝，賜錢百萬，床帳簟褥自副。

translations.literal: With folding-stool and staff not attending court; bestowed one million cash; bed curtains, bamboo mats, bedding self-attached.
translations.idiomatic: He need not attend court; he receives a million cash, with bed-curtains, fine mats, and bedding supplied."

sentences.zh: 以舍人四人為劇陽子舍人，置官騎十人。

translations.literal: With four chamberlains as householders to the Viscount of Ji, establish official riders ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Four chamberlains shall attend him as householders of the viscount of Ji, with ten mounted escorts."

sentences.zh: 使光祿勳奉策，主者詳案典禮，令皆如舊制。

translations.literal: Cause the Master of Ceremonies to bear the rescript; those in charge shall in detail examine canonical rites, ordering all like old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Let the master of ceremonies present the rescript, and let the bureaus review the statutes so every detail follows precedent."

sentences.zh: 」於是賜安車駟馬，門施行馬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was bestowed secure carriage and four-horse team; at the gate was applied riding horse block.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted a secure carriage and four-horse team, and a mounting-block was set at his gate.

sentences.zh: 舒為事必先行而後言，遜位之際，莫有知者。

translations.literal: Shu in doing affairs always first acted and afterward spoke; at the juncture of yielding position, there was none who knew.
translations.idiomatic: Shu always acted before he spoke; when he resigned, no one had seen it coming.

sentences.zh: 時論以為晉興以來，三公能辭榮善終者，未之有也。

translations.literal: Contemporary discussion held that since Jin's rise, among Three Dukes able to decline glory and end well, there had not been such.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that since the founding of Jin no holder of the three highest posts had refused honor and finished his career with such dignity.

sentences.zh: 司空衛瓘與舒書曰：「每與足下共論此事，日日未果，可謂瞻之在前，忽焉在後矣。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote Shu a letter, saying, "Whenever with you I together discussed this matter, day by day not yet fruit — it may be called 'it seemed before the eyes, suddenly afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote him, "We spoke of this again and again yet never settled it—truly it was always 'right before our eyes,' then 'gone in an instant,' as the saying goes."

sentences.zh: 」太熙元年薨，時年八十二。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Taixi he died; at the time his years were eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Taixi, aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝甚傷悼，賵賻優厚，諡曰康。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly mourned; funeral gifts were generous and thick; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply, sent lavish funeral gifts, and gave him the posthumous name Kang, "Peaceful."

sentences.zh: 子混，字延廣，清惠有才行，為太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Hun, courtesy name Yanguang, was pure, kind, had conduct and talent, and was householder to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hun, courtesy name Yanguang, was clear-minded, kind, and capable, and served as household gentleman to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，先舒卒，朝野咸為舒悲惜。

translations.literal: His years twenty-seven, he predeceased Shu; court and wild all for Shu were sorrowful and pained.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-seven, before his father, and court and countryside alike pitied Shu.

sentences.zh: 舒每哀慟，退而歎曰：「吾不及莊生遠矣，豈以無益自損乎！

translations.literal: Shu each time mourned bitterly, withdrew and sighed, saying, "I fall short of Master Zhuang by far; how could I by what brings no benefit harm myself!
translations.idiomatic: Shu mourned bitterly, then withdrew and sighed, "I am no Zhuangzi; why should I tear myself apart over what cannot help?"

sentences.zh: 」於是終服不復哭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon to the end of mourning he did not again weep.
translations.idiomatic: After that he observed the full mourning period but wept no more.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「舒惟一子，薄命短折。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Shu had only one son; thin fate, short broken.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran, "Shu had but one son, and fate cut him off in his prime."

sentences.zh: 舒告老之年，處窮獨之苦，每念怛然，為之嗟悼。

translations.literal: In the years Shu announced old age, he dwells in utter loneliness' suffering; each time I think of it I am moved and for him sigh in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Shu has asked to retire, he endures the bitterness of utter loneliness; whenever I think of it my heart aches for him."

sentences.zh: 思所以散愁養氣，可更增滋味品物。

translations.literal: Think by what to scatter sorrow and nurture qi; can further increase flavors and kinds of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Find ways to lift his spirits and strengthen him—send richer foods and finer goods."

sentences.zh: 仍給賜陽燧四望繐窗戶皁輪車牛一乘，庶出入觀望，或足散憂也。

translations.literal: Still grant him a sun-mirror four-view cord-window black-wheeled carriage oxen one team, so that going out and looking about may perhaps suffice to scatter sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him besides a four-windowed carriage with bronze fittings, corded blinds, black hubs, and a yoke of oxen, so that riding out to see the world may ease his grief."

sentences.zh: 」以庶孫融嗣。

translations.literal: " They made his grandson by a concubine, Rong, heir.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rong, born to a concubine's line, was named heir.

sentences.zh: 又早卒，從孫晃嗣。

translations.literal: Again he died young; a great-grandson by a junior line, Huang, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also died young, and a cousin's grandson, Huang, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 李憙，字季和，上黨銅鞮人也。

translations.literal: Li Xi, courtesy name Jihe, was a man of Tongdi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, whose courtesy name was Jihe, came from Tongdi in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 父牷，漢大鴻臚。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Han Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His father had served the Han as grand herald.

sentences.zh: 憙少有高行，博學研精，與北海管甯以賢良征，不行。

translations.literal: Xi from youth had high conduct, broad learning and refined study; with Guan Ning of Beihai by Worthy and Good he was summoned, and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xi showed noble character, wide learning, and exacting scholarship; he and Guan Ning of Beihai were summoned as men of worth and virtue, but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 累辟三府，不就。

translations.literal: Repeatedly the Three Offices summoned him; he did not go to office.
translations.idiomatic: The three highest offices summoned him repeatedly, yet he never took a post.

sentences.zh: 宣帝復辟憙為太傅屬，固辭疾，郡縣扶輿上道，時憙母疾篤，乃竊逾泫氏城而徒還，遂遭母喪，論者嘉其志節。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan again summoned Xi as retainer to the Grand Tutor; he firmly declined citing illness; county and commandery supported him in a litter onto the road; at the time Xi's mother was gravely ill; he then secretly crossed beyond Xuanshi city and walked back, whereupon he encountered his mother's mourning; those who discussed praised his will and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan summoned him again as an aide to the grand tutor; he pleaded illness, but county and commandery officers lifted him into a litter and forced him onto the road. His mother lay dying, so he slipped past Xuanshi and walked home, where he was able to mourn her passing; commentators praised his resolve.

sentences.zh: 後為并州別駕，時驍騎將軍秦朗過并州，州將畢軌敬焉。

translations.literal: Later he became Bing Province staff administrator; at the time General of Agile Cavalry Qin Lang passed through Bing Province, and the provincial commander Bi Gui honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became senior administrator of Bing Province when General of Agile Cavalry Qin Lang passed through the region; the provincial commander Bi Gui treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 令乘車至閣。

translations.literal: He ordered him to ride a carriage to the gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xi ride in a carriage right up to the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 憙固諫以為不可，軌不得已從之。

translations.literal: Xi firmly remonstrated, holding it impermissible; Gui having no choice followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued strenuously that this was improper, and Bi Gui, unable to refuse, yielded.

sentences.zh: 景帝輔政，命憙為大將軍從事中郎，憙到，引見，謂憙曰：「昔先公辟君而君不應，今孤命君而君至，何也？

translations.literal: Prince Jing assisted governance, ordered Xi as aide to the Grand General; Xi arrived, was led in audience, and was told to Xi, "Formerly my late father summoned you and you did not respond; now I order you and you have come — why?
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jing of Wei directed the government, he named Xi aide to the grand general. At their first audience he asked, "My father once called you to office and you stayed away; now I summon you and you appear—what has changed?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「先君以禮見待，憙得以禮進退。

translations.literal: " He replied, saying, "The former lord by ritual treated me; Xi was able by ritual to advance or withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Xi replied, "Your father treated me with courtesy, so I could accept or decline according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 明公以法見繩，憙畏法而至。

translations.literal: The enlightened lord by law sees me bound; Xi fears the law and therefore came.
translations.idiomatic: You hold me to the law; I came because I fear the law."

sentences.zh: 」帝甚重之。

translations.literal: " The prince greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince thought all the more highly of him.

sentences.zh: 轉司馬，尋拜右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred marshal, and shortly was appointed Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to marshal, then soon named chief clerk on the right.

sentences.zh: 從討毌丘儉還，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Guanqiu Jian and returning, he was promoted Palace Assistant Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the expedition against Guanqiu Jian he was promoted to palace assistant secretary.

sentences.zh: 當官正色，不憚強禦，百僚震肅焉。

translations.literal: Holding office with correct demeanor, he did not fear the powerful; the hundred officials were awed and stern.
translations.idiomatic: In office he kept a straight face and did not flinch from the mighty, so the whole bureaucracy stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 薦樂安孫璞，亦以道德顯，時人稱為知人。

translations.literal: He recommended Sun Pu of Le'an, who also by virtue and the Way was eminent; men of the time called him one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Sun Pu of Le'an, another man who won fame for integrity, and contemporaries praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大司馬，以公事免。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted Grand Marshal, and because of public affairs was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he rose to grand marshal, then lost the post over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 司馬伷為甯北將軍，鎮鄴，以憙為軍司。

translations.literal: Sima Zhou was Pacify-the-North General, garrisoned Ye, and appointed Xi army director.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhou served as pacify-the-north general at Ye, he named Xi director of the army.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除涼州刺史，加揚威將軍、假節，領護羌校尉，綏禦華夷，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Inspector of Liangzhou, added General Who Spreads Might, with credential staff, concurrently Protector-General of the Qiang, pacifying and controlling Chinese and barbarians, and had very much reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became inspector of Liangzhou with the added titles of general who spreads might and protector-general of the Qiang, bearing the credential staff; he kept peace among Chinese and tribesmen and earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 羌虜犯塞，憙因其隙會，不及啟聞，輒以便宜出軍深入，遂大克獲，以功重免譴，時人比之漢朝馮、甘焉。

translations.literal: Qiang bandits violated the passes; Xi because of their gap and opportunity, before there was time to report upward, then on his own authority sent the army deep in, whereupon there was great capture; because of merit severity of blame was remitted; men of the time compared him to Feng and Gan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang raiders broke through the frontier, Xi seized the moment, moved troops deep into their territory without waiting for court approval, and won a major victory; his merit outweighed any rebuke, and people likened him to Feng Fengshi and Gan Yanshou of the Han.

sentences.zh: 於是請還，許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested to return; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to leave the post, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 居家月餘，拜冀州刺史，累遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Dwelling at home more than a month, he was appointed Inspector of Ji Province, by accumulated transfers became Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After a month at home he was named inspector of Ji Province and eventually metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 及魏帝告禪于晉，憙以本官行司徒事，副太尉鄭沖奉策。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor announced abdication to Jin, Xi by his original office acted Minister of Education affairs, assisting Grand Commandant Zheng Chong in bearing the rescript.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor abdicated in favor of Jin, Xi, still holding his current rank, handled the minister of education's duties and assisted Grand Commandant Zheng Chong in presenting the abdication instruments.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，封祁侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was enfeoffed marquis of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era he was enfeoffed as marquis of Qi.

sentences.zh: 憙上言：「故立進令劉友、前尚書山濤、中山王睦、故尚書僕射武陔各占官三更稻田，請免濤、睦等官。

translations.literal: Xi submitted words: "Former Establish-Advancement magistrate Liu You, former Minister Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, former Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wu Gai each occupied official three-geng paddy fields; I request dismissal of Tao, Mu, and others from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized: "The former magistrate of Lijin, Liu You, the former minister Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, and the late vice-director Wu Gai each seized several geng of government paddy; I ask that Shan Tao, Prince Mu, and the others be stripped of office."

sentences.zh: 陔已亡，請貶諡。

translations.literal: Gai already having died, I request degrading his posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gai is dead; I ask that his posthumous title be lowered."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「法者，天下取正，不避親貴，然後行耳，吾豈將枉縱其間哉！

translations.literal: " An edict said, "Law is what the realm takes as correct; not avoiding kin and nobles, afterward it is put in practice — how could I intend to bend and indulge therein!
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Law is the standard for the whole realm; it must be enforced without favor to kin or great houses—do you imagine I would twist it for anyone's sake?"

sentences.zh: 然案此事皆是友所作，侵剝百姓，以繆惑朝士。

translations.literal: Yet examining this matter, it was all You who did it, encroaching and stripping the hundred surnames, thereby falsely deluding court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the inquiry shows Liu You alone engineered the scheme, extorting the common people and deceiving the court with lies."

sentences.zh: 奸吏乃敢作此，其考竟友以懲邪佞。

translations.literal: Wicked clerks then dare do this; investigate to the end You to punish the wicked and flattering.
translations.idiomatic: For a corrupt clerk to dare such things is intolerable; try Liu You to the full penalty to warn the sycophants."

sentences.zh: 濤等不貳其過者，皆勿有所問。

translations.literal: Tao and others who did not double their faults, all shall not be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao and the rest, having no second fault, shall face no charges."

sentences.zh: 《易》稱'王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故'。

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'The king's minister, troubled, troubled — not for his body's sake.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Changes says, "The king's minister faces hardship after hardship—not for private ends."

sentences.zh: 今憙亢志在公，當官而行，可謂'邦之司直'者矣。

translations.literal: Now Xi lofty in will is in the public; holding office he acts — he may be called 'the state's straight recorder.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi has set his heart on the public good and does his duty as an officer—he is truly what the ode calls "the straight man of the state."

sentences.zh: 光武有云：'貴戚且斂手以避二鮑'。

translations.literal: Guangwu had words: 'Noble kin moreover fold hands to avoid the two Baos.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu said that even imperial in-laws "drew back their hands" for fear of the two Baos."

sentences.zh: 豈其然乎！

translations.literal: How could it be thus!
translations.idiomatic: Can that not be so again now?"

sentences.zh: 其申敕群僚，各慎所司，寬宥之恩，不可數遇也。

translations.literal: Thereby proclaim to the host of officials, each careful in what they administer; the grace of lenient pardon cannot repeatedly be encountered.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be a warning to every official to mind his charge—royal mercy is not something you can count on receiving again and again."

sentences.zh: 」憙為二代司隸，朝野稱之。

translations.literal: " Xi served as Metropolitan Commandant for two reigns; court and wild praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi served as metropolitan commandant under two dynasties, and both court and countryside praised him.

sentences.zh: 以公事免。

translations.literal: Because of public affairs he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 其年，皇太子立，以憙為太子太傅。

translations.literal: That year the heir apparent was established, and Xi was appointed Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The same year the heir apparent was installed, Xi was named his grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 自魏明帝以後，久曠東宮，制度廢闕，官司不具，詹事、左右率、庶子、中舍人諸官並未置，唯置衛率令典兵，二傅並攝眾事。

translations.literal: From Wei Mingdi afterward, long the Eastern Palace was vacant; regulations and systems were abolished and lacking, offices and bureaus were not complete; Household Superintendent, Left and Right Leaders, Household Gentlemen, Palace Gentlemen of the Household — all these offices together were not established; only was established Guard Leader command to manage troops; the two tutors together held all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Ming of Wei the eastern palace had stood empty for years; its institutions had decayed and many posts were unfilled—the household superintendent, the left and right guard leaders, the household gentlemen, the palace gentlemen, and the rest had never been appointed, and only a guard commander held the troops, so the two tutors had to oversee everything.

sentences.zh: 憙在位累年，訓道盡規。

translations.literal: Xi in position accumulated years, instruction and guidance exhausted regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xi held the post for many years, instructing the heir in every duty.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射，拜特進、光祿大夫，以年老遜位。

translations.literal: He was transferred Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, appointed Specially Advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, and because of old age yielded position.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice-director of the masters of writing, received the titles specially advanced and grand master of splendid carriage, then resigned on account of age.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「光祿大夫、特進李憙，杖德居義，當升台司。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, Specially Advanced Li Xi, leaning on virtue dwells in righteousness; ought to ascend the terrace ministry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Grand Master of Splendid Carriage and Specially Advanced Li Xi upholds virtue and cleaves to duty; he should join the highest council."

sentences.zh: 毗亮朕躬，而以年尊致仕。

translations.literal: He assists and brightens my person, yet because of years venerable has retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He has been a pillar at my side, yet advanced years have led him to retire."

sentences.zh: 雖優遊無為，可以頤神，而虛心之望，能不憮然！

translations.literal: Although leisurely ease without action can nurture the spirits, yet the expectation of an empty heart — how can one not be sorrowful!
translations.idiomatic: Leisure may nourish his spirit, yet how can I not grieve at losing the counsel I counted on?"

sentences.zh: 其因光祿之號，改假金紫，置官騎十人，賜錢五十萬，祿賜班禮，一如三司，門施行馬。」

translations.literal: Thereby following the title of Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, change to bestow gold and purple, establish official riders ten men, bestow five hundred thousand cash; stipends, gifts, and court ritual all like the Three Dukes; at the gate apply riding horse block."
translations.idiomatic: Let him keep the title of grand master of splendid carriage but add the gold seal and purple ribbon, assign ten mounted attendants, and grant five hundred thousand cash, with stipends, gifts, and court precedence equal to the Three Dukes and a mounting-block at his gate."

sentences.zh: 初，憙為僕射時，涼州虜寇邊，憙唱義遣軍討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xi was Supervisor, Liangzhou barbarians raided the border; Xi raised the cause and sent an army to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xi served as vice-director, tribesmen raided Liangzhou; he was the first to urge dispatch of an army against them.

sentences.zh: 朝士謂出兵不易，虜未足為患，竟不從之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen said sending troops was not easy, the barbarians were not sufficient to become a worry; in the end they did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials argued that mobilizing troops was difficult and the raiders no real threat, and in the end they ignored him.

sentences.zh: 後虜果大縱逸，涼州覆沒，朝廷深悔焉。

translations.literal: Later the barbarians indeed greatly ran wild; Liangzhou was overturned and lost; the court deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen then ran riot, Liangzhou collapsed, and the court bitterly regretted its refusal.

sentences.zh: 以憙清素貧儉，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Because Xi was pure, plain, poor, and frugal, he was bestowed one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xi lived plainly in real poverty, the throne sent him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及齊王攸出鎮，憙上疏諫爭，辭甚懇切。

translations.literal: When Prince You of Qi went out to garrison, Xi submitted a memorial remonstrating and disputing; the wording was very earnest and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince You of Qi was sent out to a frontier command, Xi submitted a heartfelt memorial urging the emperor to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 憙自曆仕，雖清非異眾，而家無儲積，親舊故人乃至分衣共食，未嘗私以王官。

translations.literal: Xi from his successive service, although pure was not different from the crowd, yet the household had no stored accumulation; kin, old associates, and past friends even to dividing clothes and sharing food, never privately used royal office.
translations.idiomatic: Through a long career he was honest but not ostentatious, yet he never laid up stores; with kinsmen and old friends he would even share a cloak or a meal, and never used public office for private gain.

sentences.zh: 及卒，追贈太保，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When he died, posthumously he was given Grand Guardian; his posthumous name was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously named grand guardian with the posthumous title Cheng, "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 子贊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少子儉，字仲約，曆左積弩將軍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: The younger son Jian, courtesy name Zhongyue, successively was General of the Left Strong Crossbow, Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Jian, courtesy name Zhongyue, served as general of the left strong crossbowmen and as colonel of garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 儉子弘，字世彥，少有清節，永嘉末，曆給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jian's son Hong, courtesy name Shiyan, from youth had pure integrity; at the end of Yongjia, successively was Palace Attendant to the Yellow Gates, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Hong, courtesy name Shiyan, showed moral clarity from youth; late in the Yongjia era he served as palace attendant at the yellow gates and as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 劉寔，字子真，平原高唐人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a man of Gaotang in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a native of Gaotang in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢濟北惠王壽之後也，父廣，斥丘令。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Han Prince Hui of Jibei, Shou; his father Guang was magistrate of Chiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He descended from Prince Hui of Jibei, named Shou, under the Han; his father Guang had been magistrate of Chiqiu.

sentences.zh: 寔少貧苦，賣牛衣以自給。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was poor and bitter, selling cattle straw cloaks to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in grinding poverty and sold winter straw mats for cattle to keep himself fed.

sentences.zh: 然好學，手約繩，口誦書，博通古今。

translations.literal: Yet he loved learning, hand grasping cord, mouth chanting books, broadly penetrating ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved study, knotting cord to tally his lessons while he recited texts aloud, until he mastered the classical corpus past and present.

sentences.zh: 清身潔己，行無瑕玷。

translations.literal: He purified the body and cleansed himself; conduct had no flaw or stain.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his person and conduct spotless, without a blemish on his record.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，州舉秀才，皆不行。

translations.literal: The commandery investigated him Filial and Incorrupt, the province raised him Flourishing Talent; all he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt and the province as flourishing talent; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 以計吏入洛，調為河南尹丞，遷尚書郎、廷尉正。

translations.literal: As accounts clerk he entered Luoyang, was transferred Assistant to the Intendant of Henan, promoted Secretariat gentleman, Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Luoyang as a commandery accounts clerk, was transferred to assistant intendant of Henan, then rose to gentleman of the masters of writing and director in the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 後曆吏部郎，參文帝相國軍事，封循陽子。

translations.literal: Later he successively was Personnel Ministry gentleman, participated in Prince Wen's chancellor of state military affairs, and was enfeoffed viscount of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as personnel ministry gentleman, joined the military staff of Prince Wen's chancellery, and was enfeoffed as viscount of Xun.

sentences.zh: 鐘會、鄧艾之伐蜀也，有客問寔曰：「二將其平蜀乎？

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai campaigned against Shu, a guest asked Shi, saying, "The two generals — will they pacify Shu?
translations.idiomatic: During Zhong Hui and Deng Ai's invasion of Shu, a visitor asked Liu Shi, "Will those two generals conquer Shu?"

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「破蜀必矣，而皆不還。

translations.literal: " Shi said, "Breaking Shu is certain, yet both will not return.
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "They will break Shu, yet neither will come back alive."

sentences.zh: 」客問其故，笑而不答，竟如其言。

translations.literal: " The guest asked the reason; he laughed and did not answer; in the end it was as his words.
translations.idiomatic: When pressed for his reasons he only smiled and said nothing—and events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 寔之先見，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Shi's foresight was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His foresight was often of this order.

sentences.zh: 以世多進趣，廉遜道闕，乃著《崇讓論》以矯之。

translations.literal: Because the age had much advancing and rushing, the way of integrity and yielding was lacking, therefore he composed "Treatise on Honoring Yielding" to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his contemporaries scramble for advancement while modesty vanished, he wrote the "Treatise on Honoring Yielding" to set matters right.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words said:
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王之化天下，所以貴讓者，欲以出賢才，息爭競也。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings' transforming the realm — the reason they honored yielding was that they wished thereby to bring forth worthy talent and rest striving and competition.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old transformed the world by honoring deference because they wanted worthy men to come forward and strife to fall silent.

sentences.zh: 夫人情莫不欲已之賢也，故勸令讓賢以自明賢也，豈假讓不賢哉！

translations.literal: As for human feeling, none does not wish himself worthy; therefore they urged ordering yielding worthies thereby to self-manifest worthiness — how was it feigned yielding to the unworthy!
translations.idiomatic: Every man wishes to be thought worthy, so the sage kings urged men to yield place to the better qualified and thus prove their own worth—never to pretend humility while yielding to the unworthy!"

sentences.zh: 故讓道興，賢能之人不求而自出矣，至公之舉自立矣，百官之副亦豫具矣。

translations.literal: Therefore when the way of yielding rises, worthy and able men without seeking come forth of themselves; utmost impartial selection stands of itself; the hundred officials' deputies are also prepared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding is honored, able men step forward unbidden, the most impartial choices make themselves, and the whole chain of secondary offices fills of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 一官缺，擇眾官所讓最多者而用之，審之道也。

translations.literal: When one office is vacant, choose among the host of officials the one whom most have yielded to and use him — this is the way of carefulness.
translations.idiomatic: When a post opens, appoint the man to whom the greatest number of colleagues have already deferred—that is the sure way to choose well."

sentences.zh: 在朝之士相讓於上，草廬之人咸皆化之，推賢讓能之風從此生矣。

translations.literal: Gentlemen at court yield to one another above; men in thatched huts all are transformed by it; the wind of pushing worthies and yielding to ability from this arises.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers defer to one another before the throne, recluses take the lesson from them, and a wind of recommending the worthy and yielding to the able springs up everywhere."

sentences.zh: 為一國所讓，則一國士也；

translations.literal: If by one state yielded to, then he is that state's gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: The man a whole state agrees to honor is that state's true gentleman;

sentences.zh: 天下所共推，則天下士也。

translations.literal: if by the realm jointly pushed, then he is the realm's gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: the man the whole realm presses forward is the gentleman of the realm."

sentences.zh: 推讓之風行，則賢與不肖灼然殊矣。

translations.literal: When the wind of pushing yielding is practiced, then worthy and unworthy are scorchingly distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Once yielding becomes the fashion, worthy and unworthy stand out as clearly as fire and ice."

sentences.zh: 此道之行，在上者無所用其心，因成清議，隨之而已。

translations.literal: When this way is practiced, those above have no need to use their hearts; thereby pure discussion is completed, and they follow it only.
translations.idiomatic: Under such a system those on high need not scheme; pure public opinion takes shape of itself, and they have only to follow it."

sentences.zh: 故曰，蕩蕩乎堯之為君，莫之能名。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, vast vast was Yao as lord — none could name him.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying, "Vast was Yao as ruler—no one could put a name to his art."

sentences.zh: 言天下自安矣，不見堯所以化之，故不能名也。

translations.literal: It means the realm was self-at peace; they did not see whereby Yao transformed it, therefore could not name it.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace of itself; people could not point to what Yao had done to change them, and so they could not describe his government."

sentences.zh: 又曰，舜禹之有天下而不與焉，無為而化者其舜也歟。

translations.literal: Again it is said, Shun and Yu had the realm yet did not participate therein; by non-action transforming — was it not Shun!
translations.idiomatic: It is also said that Shun and Yu possessed the empire yet seemed not to grasp it; perhaps Shun was the one who ruled without acting."

sentences.zh: 賢人相讓于朝，大才之人恆在大官，小人不爭於野，天下無事矣。

translations.literal: Worthy men yield to one another at court; great-talent men always are in great offices; petty men do not contend in the wilds; the realm has no affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men defer to one another at court, great talent always fills high office, petty men do not squabble in the countryside, and the realm is untroubled."

sentences.zh: 以賢才化無事，至道興矣。

translations.literal: By worthy talent transforming to no affairs, the utmost Way rises.
translations.idiomatic: When worthies bring about an age without crises, the highest Way prevails."

sentences.zh: 已仰其成，復何與焉！

translations.literal: Already looking up to its completion, what further participation!
translations.idiomatic: The ruler has only to trust the outcome—what need has he to meddle?"

sentences.zh: 故可以歌《南風》之詩，彈五弦之琴也。

translations.literal: Therefore he could sing the "South Wind" poem, pluck the five-stringed zither.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he could sing the "South Wind" and strum the five-string lute in peace."

sentences.zh: 成此功者非有他，崇讓之所致耳。

translations.literal: Completing this achievement had nothing else; it was what honoring yielding brought about only.
translations.idiomatic: No other art produced that achievement—only the honoring of yielding did."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，能以禮讓為國，則不難也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, if able by ritual yielding to govern the state, then it is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "To govern a state by ritual and deference presents no difficulty."

sentences.zh: 在朝之人不務相讓久矣，天下化之。

translations.literal: Men at court long have not exerted themselves in yielding to one another; the realm has been transformed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers have long ceased to practice mutual deference, and the whole realm has taken its tone from them.

sentences.zh: 自魏代以來，登進辟命之士，及在職之吏，臨見受敘，雖自辭不能，終莫肯讓有勝己者。

translations.literal: From Wei times onward, gentlemen who ascended in advancement and summons appointments, and clerks in office, facing audience and receiving order, although themselves declining inability, to the end none were willing to yield to those who surpassed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei era, every man summoned to office or promoted on appointment, even when he protests his unfitness, still refuses in the end to yield to anyone better qualified.

sentences.zh: 夫推讓之風息，爭競之心生。

translations.literal: When the wind of pushing yielding ceases, the mind of striving and competition arises.
translations.idiomatic: When deference dies, the scramble for place begins.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，上興讓則下不爭，明讓不興下必爭也。

translations.literal: Confucius said, when those above raise yielding then those below do not contend; it clarifies that when yielding does not rise, those below must contend.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "When superiors honor yielding, inferiors do not fight among themselves"—which shows that without yielding below, contention is inevitable."

sentences.zh: 推讓之道興，則賢能之人日見推舉；

translations.literal: When the way of pushing yielding rises, then worthy and able men day by day are seen pushed and raised;
translations.idiomatic: When yielding prevails, able men are advanced every day;

sentences.zh: 爭競之心生，則賢能之人日見謗毀。

translations.literal: when the mind of striving and competition arises, then worthy and able men day by day are seen slandered and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: when contention rules, they are slandered every day."

sentences.zh: 夫爭者之欲自先，甚惡能者之先，不能無毀也。

translations.literal: As for contenders' desire to put themselves first, they greatly hate able men's going first; they cannot be without destruction.
translations.idiomatic: A man who fights for precedence loathes anyone ahead of him who is more capable, and slander follows inevitably."

sentences.zh: 故孔墨不能免世之謗己，況不及孔墨者乎！

translations.literal: Therefore even Kong and Mo could not escape the age's slandering them, how much more those who do not reach Kong and Mo!
translations.idiomatic: Even Confucius and Mozi could not escape slander—what hope have lesser men?"

sentences.zh: 議者僉然言，世少高名之才，朝廷不有大才之人可以為大官者。

translations.literal: Discussers all alike say, the age lacks high-named talent; the court does not have great-talent men who can become great officials.
translations.idiomatic: Critics all insist that the age lacks men of towering reputation and that the court has no great talent fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 山澤人小官吏亦復雲，朝廷之士雖有大官名德，皆不及往時人也。

translations.literal: Mountain-marsh men and petty clerks also again say, court gentlemen although they have great office name and virtue, all do not reach men of former times.
translations.idiomatic: Rustics and petty clerks echo the charge that today's grandees, however eminent their titles, fall short of men of earlier generations.

sentences.zh: 餘以為此二言皆失之矣。

translations.literal: I hold that these two sayings both miss it.
translations.idiomatic: Both judgments miss the mark.

sentences.zh: 非時獨乏賢也，時不貴讓。

translations.literal: It is not that the age alone lacks worthies; the age does not honor yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is not a sudden dearth of worthies but that the age no longer esteems yielding.

sentences.zh: 一人有先眾之譽，毀必隨之，名不得成使之然也。

translations.literal: When one man has reputation ahead of the crowd, destruction must follow him; names cannot be completed — this makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: Let a single man win praise above the rest, and malice dogs his steps; no good name can stand under such pressure.

sentences.zh: 雖令稷契復存，亦不復能全其名矣。

translations.literal: Even if Ji and Xie again lived, they also could not again complete their names.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Ji and Xie walked the earth again, they could not keep their reputations intact.

sentences.zh: 能否混雜，優劣不分，士無素定之價，官職有缺，主選之吏不知所用，但案官次而舉之。

translations.literal: Able and unable are mixed in confusion, excellence and inferiority are not divided; gentlemen have no plain-settled price; when offices have vacancies, masters of selection clerks do not know whom to use, but only examine official order and raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Able and useless are jumbled together with no clear ranking, so gentlemen carry no settled market value; when a vacancy opens, the appointing clerk has no idea whom to choose and simply promotes the next man in line.

sentences.zh: 同才之人先用者，非勢家之子，則必為有勢者之所念也。

translations.literal: Among men of same talent, those first used are either not sons of powerful houses, then they must be those whom the powerful think of.
translations.idiomatic: Among equals the first to win appointment is either a son of the mighty or a protégé of the mighty.

sentences.zh: 非能獨賢，因其先用之資，而復遷之無已。

translations.literal: It is not that they alone are worthy; because of their first-used capital, again they are transferred without end.
translations.idiomatic: Not because they alone deserve it, but because early preferment becomes a ladder of endless promotions.

sentences.zh: 遷之無已，不勝其任之病發矣。

translations.literal: Transferring without end, the sickness of not bearing their duties arises.
translations.idiomatic: Promote such men without end and you soon see them collapse under duties they cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 觀在官之人，政績無聞，自非勢家之子，率多因資次而進也。

translations.literal: Observe men in office: administrative achievement is unheard of; if they are not self-wise sons of powerful houses, mostly many advance because of qualifications in order.
translations.idiomatic: Look at officials today: few have any record of real achievement; unless they are sons of great houses, they have usually climbed sheerly by seniority.

sentences.zh: 向令天下貴讓，士必由於見讓而後名成，名成而官乃得用之。

translations.literal: Suppose we ordered the realm to honor yielding; gentlemen must by being seen yielded to afterward complete their names, names completed and then offices could use them.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the realm honored deference: a man would first win recommendation through others' yielding to him, build a reputation on that, and only then receive appointment.

sentences.zh: 諸名行不立之人，在官無政績之稱，讓之者必矣，官無因得而用之也。

translations.literal: The various men whose names and conduct are not established, in office have no praise of administrative achievement — those who yield to them will be certain; offices have no cause thereby to use them.
translations.idiomatic: Men of no established reputation who leave no record of achievement in office would find plenty of colleagues ready to yield to them, and no bureau could justify hiring them.

sentences.zh: 所以見用不息者，由讓道廢，因資用人之有失久矣。

translations.literal: The reason those seen employed without cease is because the way of yielding was abolished; relying on seniority to employ men has missed the mark for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The endless parade of unfit appointees comes from the death of yielding and from long reliance on seniority instead of merit.

sentences.zh: 故自漢魏以來，時開大舉，令眾官各舉所知，唯才所任，不限階次，如此者甚數矣。

translations.literal: Therefore from Han and Wei onward, times opened great selections, ordering the host of officials each to raise those they knew, only talent being entrusted, not limited by rank order — such cases have been very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei the court has often ordered a general nomination: every official recommends men he knows, with talent the sole criterion and rank ignored—such campaigns have been many.

sentences.zh: 其所舉必有當者，不聞時有擢用，不知何誰最賢故也。

translations.literal: Among those raised there must be suitable ones, yet we do not hear timely promotions and selections — because we do not know who is most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees must be suitable, yet we never hear of timely promotions from these lists—because no one can tell who is truly the best.

sentences.zh: 所舉必有不當，而罪不加，不知何誰最不肖也。

translations.literal: Among those raised there must be unsuitable ones, yet punishment is not applied — because we do not know who is most unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees must be unsuitable, yet no one is punished—because no one can tell who is the worst.

sentences.zh: 所以不可得知，由當時之人莫肯相推，賢愚之名不別，令其如此。

translations.literal: The reason it cannot be known is because men of the time none were willing to defer to one another; names of worthy and foolish are not distinguished, ordering it to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that contemporaries will not recommend one another, worthy and foolish look alike, and the system ends in this confusion.

sentences.zh: 舉者知在上者察不能審，故敢漫舉而進之。

translations.literal: Those who raise know those above examine yet cannot be careful; therefore they dare carelessly to raise and advance them.
translations.idiomatic: Nominators know superiors cannot vet every name, so they toss lists together without care.

sentences.zh: 或舉所賢，因及所念，一頓而至，人數猥多，各言所舉者賢，加之高狀，相似如一，難得而分矣。

translations.literal: Some raise those they esteem, thereby reaching those they favor; in one batch they arrive, the number of persons very many; each says those he raised are worthy, adding them high descriptions, similar as one — hard to obtain and divide.
translations.idiomatic: Some push their favorites and tag along their cronies; names arrive in heaps, every sponsor swears his pick is brilliant and piles on the same lofty phrases, so the court cannot sort them out.

sentences.zh: 參錯相亂，真偽同貫，更復由此而甚。

translations.literal: Mixed and crossed they mutually confuse; true and false share one string; again from this it becomes extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and falsehood are jumbled in one bundle, and the tangle only grows worse.

sentences.zh: 雖舉者不能盡忠之罪，亦由上開聽察之路濫，令其爾也。

translations.literal: Although it is also the nominators' crime of not exhausting loyalty, it is also because those above opened the road of listening and examining to flood, ordering it to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: Nominators share the blame for disloyalty, yet the throne has opened so wide a gate for rumor that the mess was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 昔齊王好聽竽聲，必令三百人合吹而後聽之，廩以數人之俸。

translations.literal: Formerly the King of Qi loved listening to yu pipes, and always ordered three hundred men jointly to blow before he listened, granarying them several men's stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Once the King of Qi loved the sound of the yu and insisted that three hundred players blow together before he would listen, paying them the rations of several men each.

sentences.zh: 南郭先生不知吹竽者也，以三百人合吹可以容其不知，因請為王吹竽，虛食數人之俸。

translations.literal: Master Nanguo was one who did not know how to blow the yu; because three hundred men jointly blowing could contain his not knowing, therefore he requested to blow yu for the king, vainly eating several men's stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Master Nanguo of the southern suburb could not play at all, but hid inside a chorus of three hundred and drew several men's pay for doing nothing.

sentences.zh: 嗣王覺而改之，難彰先王之過。

translations.literal: The succeeding king perceived and changed it, finding it hard to display the former king's fault.
translations.idiomatic: When the new king saw through the trick, he wished to reform the practice yet hesitated to shame his father.

sentences.zh: 乃下令曰：「吾之好聞竽聲有甚于先王，欲一一列而聽之。

translations.literal: Then he issued an order, saying, "My liking to hear yu sound is greater than the former king's; I wish each one in row to play and I will listen.
translations.idiomatic: So he proclaimed, "I love the yu even more than my father did; I mean to hear each musician play in turn."

sentences.zh: 」先生于此逃矣。

translations.literal: " The master at this fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that the fellow fled the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 推賢之風不立，濫舉之法不改，則南郭先生之徒盈於朝矣。

translations.literal: If the wind of pushing worthies is not established, if the law of reckless raising is not changed, then disciples of Master Nanguo fill the court.
translations.idiomatic: Until we honor real recommendation and stop indiscriminate lists, the court will swarm with Nanguos.

sentences.zh: 才高守道之士日退，馳走有勢之門日多矣。

translations.literal: Men of high talent who keep the Way daily withdraw; those who gallop to powerful gates daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men who keep their integrity withdraw further each day, while toadies at great houses grow more numerous.

sentences.zh: 雖國有典刑，弗能禁矣。

translations.literal: Although the state has statutes and punishments, it cannot forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Even the full code cannot check it.

sentences.zh: 夫讓道不興之弊，非徒賢人在下位，不得時進也，國之良臣荷重任者，亦將以漸受罪退矣。

translations.literal: The harm when the way of yielding does not rise is not only that worthy men in lower positions cannot advance in time; the state's good ministers bearing heavy burden also will by degrees suffer blame and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding dies, the harm is not only that able men stuck below cannot rise; even good ministers who bear the heaviest burdens will step by step be hounded from office.

sentences.zh: 何以知其然也？

translations.literal: By what do we know it is so?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know this is true?

sentences.zh: 孔子以為顏氏之子不貳過耳，明非聖人皆有過。

translations.literal: Confucius thought the Yan clan's son did not repeat faults only — it clarifies that not being sages, all have faults.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said even Yan Hui never repeated a mistake—meaning everyone short of a sage errs sometimes.

sentences.zh: 寵貴之地欲之者多矣，惡賢能者塞其路，其過而毀之者亦多矣。

translations.literal: In places of favor and nobility, those who desire them are many; those who hate worthies and able men block their road; those who for their faults destroy them are also many.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone covets high favor; rivals who hate true talent block the path, and many seize on small slips to ruin a man.

sentences.zh: 夫謗毀之生，非徒空設，必因人之微過而甚之者也。

translations.literal: As for slander and destruction arising, it is not merely empty establishment; it must be because of men's slight faults that they exaggerate them.
translations.idiomatic: Slander is never spun from thin air; it always seizes some tiny fault and blows it out of proportion.

sentences.zh: 譭謗之言數聞，在上者雖欲弗納，不能不杖所聞，因事之來而微察之也，無以，其驗至矣。

translations.literal: Words of ruinous slander repeatedly are heard; those above although they wish not to accept, cannot but lean on what they hear, because affairs come and they slightly examine them; having no other means, the verification arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When calumny is repeated often enough, the ruler may wish to ignore it yet cannot help leaning on what he hears; each new incident invites scrutiny, and in time the charges seem proved.

sentences.zh: 得其驗，安得不理其罪。

translations.literal: Having obtained the verification, how can they not handle their crimes?
translations.idiomatic: Once it looks verified, how can the throne fail to punish?

sentences.zh: 若知而縱之，王之威日衰，令之不行自此始矣。

translations.literal: If knowing yet indulging them, the king's awe daily wanes; orders not being practiced from this begin.
translations.idiomatic: To know guilt and overlook it drains royal authority and marks the moment when decrees cease to bite.

sentences.zh: 知而皆理之，受罪退者稍多，大臣有不自固之心。

translations.literal: If knowing and all handling them, those who suffer punishment and withdraw gradually become many, great ministers have hearts not self-firm.
translations.idiomatic: If every charge is prosecuted, dismissed ministers multiply and great officers lose confidence in their own survival.

sentences.zh: 夫賢才不進，貴臣日疏，此有國者之深憂也。

translations.literal: When worthy talent does not advance and honored ministers daily grow distant, this is what those who hold the state deeply worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked promotion of talent and estrangement of loyal ministers are a ruler's deepest fears.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「受祿不讓，至於已斯亡。

translations.literal: The Odes says, "Receiving emolument without yielding — to the point of self, then perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, "He took his salary without yielding—unto himself came ruin."

sentences.zh: 」不讓之人憂亡不暇，而望其益國朝，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: " Men who do not yield worry about perishing without leisure, yet hope they benefit state and court — is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Men who never yield are too busy saving their own skins to strengthen the state—can we expect much from them?"

sentences.zh: 竊以為改此俗甚易耳。

translations.literal: I privately hold that changing this custom is very easy.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this custom could be changed with ease.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: By what is it known?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 夫一時在官之人，雖雜有凡猥之才，其中賢明者亦多矣，豈可謂皆不知讓賢為貴邪！

translations.literal: As for men in office at one time, although mixed with vulgar and base talent, among them the worthy and bright are also many — how can it be said they all do not know yielding to worthies is noble!
translations.idiomatic: The men in office at any moment, though many are mediocre, include a host of able and upright men—surely they all know that yielding to the better man is the honorable course!"

sentences.zh: 直以其時皆不讓，習以成俗，故遂不為耳。

translations.literal: Straight because at that time all did not yield, habit thereby completed custom, therefore in the end they did not do it.
translations.idiomatic: They do not yield only because no one yields now; habit has frozen into custom, and so they follow along.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，皆通表上聞，名之謝章，所由來尚矣。

translations.literal: When ministers are first appointed, all pass memorials upward to be heard; naming them thanks memorials — the origin thereof is long.
translations.idiomatic: Every new appointee submits a memorial of thanks to the throne—a practice of great antiquity.

sentences.zh: 原謝章之本意，欲進賢能以謝國恩也。

translations.literal: Tracing the thanks memorial's root intent, it desired to advance worthy ability thereby to thank state grace.
translations.idiomatic: The original purpose of that memorial was to recommend worthier men in gratitude for imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 昔舜以禹為司空，禹拜稽首，讓於稷契及咎繇。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun made Yu Minister of Works; Yu bowed touching forehead, yielding to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun made Yu minister of works, Yu kowtowed and yielded the honor to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.

sentences.zh: 使益為虞官，讓於硃虎、熊、羆。

translations.literal: He made Yi forest officer, yielding to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was made warden of forests and marshes, he deferred to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.

sentences.zh: 使伯夷典三禮，讓于夔龍。

translations.literal: He made Boyi manage the three rites, yielding to Kui and Long.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyi was put in charge of the three classes of rites, he yielded to Kui and Long.

sentences.zh: 唐虞之時，眾官初除，莫不皆讓也。

translations.literal: In the time of Tang and Yu, when the host of officials were first appointed, none did not all yield.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun every first appointment was accompanied by such deferrals.

sentences.zh: 謝章之義，蓋取於此。

translations.literal: The meaning of the thanks memorial, probably was taken from this.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial of thanks took its meaning from that age.

sentences.zh: 《書》記之者，欲以永世作則。

translations.literal: The Documents records them, desiring thereby for endless ages to make a model.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents set down these acts so later ages would have a model.

sentences.zh: 季世所用，不賢不能讓賢，虛謝見用之恩而已。

translations.literal: What declining ages use: not worthy, unable to yield to worthies — empty thanks for the grace of being used only.
translations.idiomatic: In a decadent age the unworthy cannot yield to worthier men; the memorial becomes an empty gesture of thanks.

sentences.zh: 相承不變，習俗之失也。

translations.literal: Handed down unchanged — it is the loss of habit and custom.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation never changed the form—only the spirit was lost.

sentences.zh: 夫敘用之官得通章表者，其讓賢推能乃通，其不能有所讓徒費簡紙者，皆絕不通。

translations.literal: As for appointment offices that can pass memorials, if their yielding worthies and pushing ability then pass; those who cannot have anything to yield, vainly wasting bamboo slips and paper — all cut off and not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Let every bureau that may submit memorials accept only those that name worthier men to replace the writer; any memorial that yields no one and wastes paper should be rejected unread.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，各思推賢能而讓之矣，讓之文付主者掌之。

translations.literal: When ministers are first appointed, each thinks to push worthy ability and yield to them; the texts of yielding are handed to the chief keeper to hold.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment each man should propose a worthier candidate; the text of his deferral goes to the keeper of records.

sentences.zh: 三司有缺，擇三司所讓最多者而用之。

translations.literal: When the Three Dukes have a vacancy, choose among what the Three Dukes yielded to most and use him.
translations.idiomatic: When a seat among the Three Dukes falls vacant, choose the man to whom the three have most often deferred.

sentences.zh: 此為一公缺，三公已豫選之矣。

translations.literal: This is: one duke vacant, the Three Dukes have already pre-selected him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one grandee's vacancy is filled from names the three have already ranked.

sentences.zh: 且主選之吏，不必任公而選三公，不如令三公自共選一公為詳也。

translations.literal: Moreover appointment clerks need not entrust the duke to select the Three Dukes — it is not as good as ordering the Three Dukes themselves jointly to select one duke, which is more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: It is needless to charge the personnel bureau with picking the Three Dukes; better let the three jointly choose their own colleague—that is surer.

sentences.zh: 四征缺，擇四征所讓最多而用之，此為一征缺，四征已豫選之矣，必詳於停缺而令主者選四征也。

translations.literal: When a Four Expeditions post is vacant, choose among what the four expeditions yielded to most and use him; this is: one expedition vacant, the four expeditions have already pre-selected him — it must be more detailed than halting the vacancy and ordering the chief to select the four expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: When a Four Expeditions command opens, pick the man most often yielded to by the four commanders—so one vacancy is filled from lists the four have already filed, a far sounder method than leaving the post empty while some clerk picks among four nominees.

sentences.zh: 尚書缺，擇尚書所讓最多者而用之，此為八尚書共選一尚書，詳于臨缺令主者選八尚書也。

translations.literal: When a Masters of Writing post is vacant, choose among what the Masters of Writing yielded to most and use him; this is: the eight Masters of Writing jointly select one Master of Writing — more detailed than on facing vacancy ordering the chief to select eight Masters of Writing.
