translations.idiomatic: When a minister of the masters of writing is needed, take the man most deferred to by the eight ministers—eight colleagues choose one, which beats leaving a gap and letting a single clerk juggle eight names.

sentences.zh: 郡守缺，擇眾郡所讓最多者而用之，詳于任主者令選百郡守也。

translations.literal: When a commandery governor is vacant, choose among what the host of commanderies yielded to most and use him — more detailed than entrusting the chief to order selection of a hundred commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: When a commandery governorship opens, choose the man most often yielded to across the commanderies—far better than asking one appointing officer to rank a hundred magistrates.

sentences.zh: 夫以眾官百郡之讓，與主者共相比，不可同歲而論也。

translations.literal: To use the yielding of the host of officials and hundred commanderies, compared with the chief together — they cannot be spoken of in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment of hundreds of deferring officials cannot be mentioned in the same breath as one clerk's guess.

sentences.zh: 雖復令三府參舉官，本不委以舉選之任，各不能以根其心也。

translations.literal: Although again ordering the Three Offices jointly to deliberate on raising officials, fundamentally they were not entrusted with the duty of raising and selecting; each cannot thereby root his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the three bureaus are ordered to deliberate on nominations, they are not truly charged with selection, so none commits his judgment.

sentences.zh: 其所用心者裁之不二三，但令主者案官次而舉之，不用精也。

translations.literal: What they use heart on cuts it not two or three; only ordering the chief to examine official order and raise them — not using refinement.
translations.idiomatic: They give the matter a moment's thought, then tell the appointing clerk to go by seniority—no care for quality.

sentences.zh: 賢愚皆讓，百姓耳目盡為國耳目。

translations.literal: Worthy and foolish all yield; the hundred surnames' ears and eyes all become the state's ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When worthy and foolish alike must defer to someone else, every commoner's eyes and ears become the eyes and ears of the state.

sentences.zh: 夫人情爭則欲毀己所不知，讓則競推於勝己。

translations.literal: As for human feeling: when striving, then they wish to destroy what they themselves do not know; when yielding, then they compete to push toward those who surpass themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In a scramble men slander what they do not understand; in yielding they compete to lift up whoever surpasses them.

sentences.zh: 故世爭則毀譽交錯，優劣不分，難得而讓也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the age strives, praise and blame cross confused; excellence and inferiority are not divided — hard to obtain yielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the age is contentious, praise and blame tangle until no one can tell who excels—deference becomes impossible.

sentences.zh: 時讓則賢智顯出，能否之美歷歷相次，不可得而亂也。

translations.literal: When yielding in the age, then worthy wisdom appears; the beauty of able and unable is clear, succeeding in order — cannot be obtained and confused.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding is the fashion, talent stands out and able and useless line up in clear order—no confusion possible.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，能退身修已者，讓之者多矣。

translations.literal: At this time, those able to withdraw the body and cultivate themselves — those who yield to them are many.
translations.idiomatic: In such an hour, any man who steps back to cultivate himself will find many ready to yield him place.

sentences.zh: 雖欲守貧賤，不可得也。

translations.literal: Although wishing to keep poverty and low status, it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he wished to remain poor and obscure, he could not.

sentences.zh: 馳騖進趣而欲人見讓，猶卻行而求前也。

translations.literal: Galloping and rushing advancement and wishing others to see yielding to oneself — is like walking backward yet seeking forward.
translations.idiomatic: To scramble for promotion and still expect others to defer is like walking backward and hoping to advance.

sentences.zh: 夫如此，愚智咸知進身求通，非修之於己則無由矣。

translations.literal: If thus, foolish and wise alike know advancing the body and seeking penetration — if not cultivating in oneself then there is no way.
translations.idiomatic: Then fool and sage alike see that to rise they must polish themselves—there is no other road.

sentences.zh: 游外求者，於此相隨而歸矣。

translations.literal: Those who roam outside seeking — at this follow one another and return.
translations.idiomatic: Men who chase outside connections will come home to self-cultivation instead.

sentences.zh: 浮聲虛論，不禁而自息矣。

translations.literal: Floating sounds and empty discussions, without forbidding, of themselves cease.
translations.idiomatic: Empty rumor and hollow debate die away without a ban.

sentences.zh: 人人無所用其心，任眾人之議，而天下自化矣。

translations.literal: Each man has nowhere to use his heart; entrust the host of men's discussions, and the realm transforms itself.
translations.idiomatic: No one needs to scheme; trust public discussion, and the realm orders itself.

sentences.zh: 不言之化行，巍巍之美於此著矣。

translations.literal: Non-speaking transformation is practiced; the lofty beauty here is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Silent transformation takes hold, and the majesty of good rule shows forth.

sentences.zh: 讓可以致此，豈可不務之哉！

translations.literal: Yielding can bring this about — how can it not be urgently pursued!
translations.idiomatic: Yielding can achieve this—how can we fail to pursue it?"

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「范宣子之讓，其下皆讓。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Tradition says, "Fan Xuanzi's yielding — his subordinates all yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo commentary says, "When Fan Xuanzi yielded, his subordinates yielded in turn."

sentences.zh: 欒黶雖汰，弗敢違也。

translations.literal: Luan Yan although extravagant, did not dare disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Even the arrogant Luan Yan did not dare refuse."

sentences.zh: 晉國以平，數世賴之。

translations.literal: Jin state thereby was pacified; several ages relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was pacified thereby, and generations reaped the benefit."

sentences.zh: 」上世之化也，君子尚能而讓其下，小人力農以事其上，上下有禮，讒慝遠黜，由不爭也。

translations.literal: " Upper ages' transformation: the gentleman esteems ability and yields to those below; petty men exert strength in farming to serve those above; above and below have ritual; slander and evil are distantly banished — from not contending.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the transformation of high antiquity: gentlemen honored ability and deferred to inferiors, while commoners bent to the plow to serve their betters; rank observed ritual, slander and malice were driven off, and all because men did not fight for place."

sentences.zh: 及其亂也，國家之弊，恆必由之。

translations.literal: Reaching their disorder, the state's ills, always must come from this.
translations.idiomatic: When that order breaks down, the state's sickness always stems from the same cause."

sentences.zh: 篤論了了如此。

translations.literal: The firm discussion is clear thus.
translations.idiomatic: The argument stands clear as this."

sentences.zh: 在朝君子典選大官，能不以人廢言，舉而行之，各以讓賢舉能為先務，則群才猥出，能否殊別，蓋世之功，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Gentlemen at court who manage selection and great officials, if able not because of the person to discard words, raise and put them in practice, each taking yielding to worthies and raising ability as first task, then host of talents will swarm forth, able and unable will be sharply distinguished — age-surpassing achievement, nothing greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: If the great officers who control appointments will not dismiss good counsel because of its source, but put these measures into practice and make yielding to worthier men their first duty, talent will pour forth, able and useless will stand apart, and no achievement could match it for an age."

sentences.zh: 泰始初，進爵為伯，累遷少府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he advanced in noble rank to earl, by accumulated transfers became Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi his noble rank rose to earl, and he was promoted step by step to privy treasurer.

sentences.zh: 咸甯中為太常。

translations.literal: In Xianning he was Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianning era he served as minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 杜預之伐吳也，寔以本官行鎮南軍司。

translations.literal: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Shi by his original office acted South Garrisoning Army Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Liu Shi, still in his current post, served as army director on the southern pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 初，寔妻盧氏生子躋而卒，華氏將以女妻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi's wife the Lu clan bore a son Ji and died; the Hua clan was about to take a daughter and marry her to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shi's wife of the Lu clan bore a son, Ji, then died; the Hua family wished to give him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 寔弟智諫曰：「華家類貪，必破門戶。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Zhi remonstrated, saying, "The Hua clan is by kind greedy; they will surely break the household gate.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhi warned him, "The Huas are a grasping clan; they will ruin our house."

sentences.zh: 」辭之不得，竟婚華氏而生子夏。

translations.literal: " Declining it he could not obtain; in the end he married the Hua clan and bore a son Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Shi could not refuse the match; he married into the Hua family and fathered a son named Xia.

sentences.zh: 寔竟坐夏受賂，免官。

translations.literal: Shi in the end because of Xia sitting accepting bribes was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Shi lost his office because Xia took bribes.

sentences.zh: 頃之為大司農，又以夏罪免。

translations.literal: Before long he was Grand Minister of Agriculture, again because of Xia's crime dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named grand minister of agriculture, then dismissed again over Xia's crimes.

sentences.zh: 寔每還州裏，鄉人載酒肉以候之。

translations.literal: Whenever Shi returned to the commandery district, townsmen loaded wine and meat to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shi returned to his home district, villagers brought wine and meat to greet him.

sentences.zh: 寔難逆其意，輒共啖而返其餘。

translations.literal: Shi found it hard to go against their intent, then always together ate and returned the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to refuse their kindness outright, he would share a little of the feast and send the rest back.

sentences.zh: 或謂寔曰：「君行高一世，而諸子不能遵。

translations.literal: Someone said to Shi, "Your conduct is high above one age, yet the various sons cannot follow.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "Your conduct towers above the age, yet your sons will not follow your example."

sentences.zh: 何不旦夕切磋，使知過而自改邪！

translations.literal: Why not morning and evening cut and polish, causing them to know fault and themselves reform!
translations.idiomatic: Why not lecture them day and night until they see their faults and mend their ways?"

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「吾之所行，是所聞見，不相祖習，豈復教誨之所得乎！

translations.literal: " Shi said, "What I practice is what I heard and saw; we do not mutually imitate and practice — how again could instruction and teaching obtain it!
translations.idiomatic: Shi answered, "What I do rests on what I myself saw and heard; my sons have not walked the same path—how could mere lecturing reach them now?"

sentences.zh: 」世以寔言為當。

translations.literal: " The age held Shi's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time judged his reply sound.

sentences.zh: 後起為國子祭酒、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he rose as Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as libationer of the imperial academy and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子初封廣陵王，高選師友，以寔為師。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, highly selecting teachers and friends, they made Shi his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed as prince of Guangling, the court chose his tutors with care and named Shi his principal teacher.

sentences.zh: 元康初，進爵為侯，累遷太子太保，加侍中、特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領冀州都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he advanced in noble rank to marquis, by accumulated transfers became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, added Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of the Right of Splendid Carriage, Opener of Office with parity of the Three Dukes, concurrently Area Commander of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang his rank rose to marquis; he rose through junior tutor to the heir apparent to the added titles of palace attendant, specially advanced, grand master of the right of splendid carriage, and opener of a bureau with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, while commanding military affairs in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 九年，策拜司空，遷太保，轉太傅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was rescript-appointed Minister of Works, transferred Grand Guardian, transferred Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the era he received the rescript as minister of works, then moved up to grand guardian and finally grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 太安初，寔以老病遜位，賜安車駟馬、錢百萬，以侯就第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tai'an, Shi because of old age and illness yielded position; he was bestowed secure carriage and four-horse team, one million cash, and as marquis went to mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tai'an era he resigned on grounds of age and illness; the court granted him a secure carriage, four-horse team, a million cash, and permission to retire to his mansion as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 及長沙成都之相攻也，寔為軍人所掠，潛歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Changsha and Chengdu mutually attacked, Shi was plundered by soldiers and secretly returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes of Changsha and Chengdu turned on each other, soldiers plundered him and he slipped away to his home district.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「昔虞任五臣，致垂拱之化，漢相蕭何，興寧一之譽，故能光隆於當時，垂裕於百代。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict said, "Formerly Yu employed five ministers, achieving draped-arms transformation; Han minister Xiao He, raised quiet-oneness' praise; therefore able to shine grand in their time, hang abundance for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict declared, "Ancient Shun ruled through five ministers and achieved the government of folded hands; Han's chancellor Xiao He brought an age of unity and calm—thus they shone in their own day and left an example for a hundred generations."

sentences.zh: 朕紹天明命，臨御萬邦，所以崇顯政道者，亦賴之於元臣庶尹，畢力股肱，以副至望。

translations.literal: I continue Heaven's bright mandate, face and govern the myriad regions; the means by which to exalt and display the way of government, also rely on these chief ministers and many directors, exhausting strength in arms and thighs, to match utmost expectation.
translations.idiomatic: I have received Heaven's mandate to rule the myriad regions; to exalt the way of government I depend on great ministers and heads of office who give their full strength as my arms and legs, answering my deepest hopes."

sentences.zh: 而君年耆告老，確然難違。

translations.literal: Yet you, lord, in years old announce old age; firmly it is hard to go against.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you, venerable in years, have asked to retire, and your resolve cannot lightly be set aside."

sentences.zh: 今聽君以侯就第，位居三司之上，秩祿准舊，賜几杖不朝及宅一區。

translations.literal: Now I listen to you, lord, as marquis to go to mansion; position placed above the Three Dukes; rank and emolument accord with the old; bestow folding-stool and staff, not attending court, and one mansion plot.
translations.idiomatic: I grant you, lord, to retire to your mansion as a marquis with standing above the Three Dukes, stipend as before, the gift of a folding-stool and staff exempting you from court, and one residence.

sentences.zh: 國之大政，將就諮於君，副朕意焉。

translations.literal: The state's great policies will go to consult with you, lord, matching my intent.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty affairs of state I shall still seek your counsel, that you may answer my deepest purpose."

sentences.zh: 」歲余薨，時年九十一，諡曰元。

translations.literal: " After a little more than a year he died; at the time his years were ninety-one; his posthumous name was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died, aged ninety-one, with the posthumous name Yuan, "Primal."

sentences.zh: 寔少貧窶，杖策徒行，每所憩止，不累主人，薪水之事，皆自營給。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was poor and mean; staff and plan, walking on foot; each place he rested, he did not burden the host; firewood and water matters, all he himself supplied.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shi was destitute; leaning on a staff he went on foot, and wherever he lodged he imposed no burden on his host, gathering his own firewood and water.

sentences.zh: 及位望通顯，每崇儉素，不尚華麗。

translations.literal: When position and repute were thorough and eminent, he always honored frugality and plainness, did not esteem splendor and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Even when rank and fame were at their height he clung to plain frugality and scorned display.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣石崇家，如廁，見有絳紋帳，裀褥甚麗，兩婢持香囊。

translations.literal: Once he went to Shi Chong's house, entered the privy, and saw there were crimson-patterned curtains, cushions and bedding very beautiful, two maids holding incense pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Shi Chong's house he stepped into what he thought was a lavatory and found crimson brocade curtains, sumptuous mats, and two maids bearing sachets of incense.

sentences.zh: 寔便退，笑謂崇曰：「誤入卿內。

translations.literal: Shi then withdrew, laughed and said to Chong, "I mistakenly entered your inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi drew back at once and said with a smile, "I have blundered into your private rooms."

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「是廁耳。

translations.literal: " Chong said, "It is the privy only.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "That is the privy."

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「貧士未嘗得此。

translations.literal: " Shi said, "A poor scholar has never obtained this.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "A poor scholar like me has never seen such a privy."

sentences.zh: 」乃更如他廁。

translations.literal: " Then he again went to another privy.
translations.idiomatic: He asked directions to an ordinary latrine instead.

sentences.zh: 雖處榮寵，居無第宅，所得俸祿，贍恤親故。

translations.literal: Although dwelling in glory and favor, he had no mansion house; what stipend he obtained, he relieved and aided kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Though he stood high in favor, he owned no grand mansion and spent his salary supporting kinsmen and old friends.

sentences.zh: 雖禮教陵遲，而行己以正。

translations.literal: Although ritual teaching declined and lagged, in conducting himself he used the straight.
translations.idiomatic: Even as public morals slackened, he kept his own conduct upright.

sentences.zh: 喪妻為廬杖之制，終喪不禦內。

translations.literal: On losing his wife he made the hut-and-staff system; to the end of mourning he did not take the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife died he observed the mourning hut and staff rites and took no concubine until the mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 輕薄者笑之，寔不以介意。

translations.literal: Frivolous men laughed at him; Shi did not on that account take it to mind.
translations.idiomatic: Wits mocked him for it, but he paid them no heed.

sentences.zh: 自少及老，篤學不倦，雖居職務，卷弗離手。

translations.literal: From youth to old age he loved learning without weariness; although occupying official duties, scrolls did not leave his hand.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he studied tirelessly; even in office he never laid down his books.

sentences.zh: 尤精《三傳》，辨正《公羊》，以為衛輒不應辭以王父命，祭仲失為臣之節，舉此二端以明臣子之體，遂行於世。

translations.literal: He was especially refined in the Three Traditions, discriminating and correcting the Gongyang, holding that Wei Kuaire ought not to have declined citing grandfather's command, that Zhai Zhong lost a minister's integrity; raising these two ends to clarify minister-and-son's substance, it then was practiced in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn and corrected the Gongyang tradition, arguing that Prince Kuaire of Wei should not have refused the throne citing his grandfather's order and that Zhai Zhong had failed a minister's duty; by these two cases he defined the proper relation of subject to ruler, and his reading won wide acceptance.

sentences.zh: 又撰《春秋條例》二十卷。

translations.literal: Again he composed Spring and Autumn Regulations and Cases in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled twenty fascicles of Spring and Autumn precedents and principles.

sentences.zh: 有二子，躋、夏。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Ji and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Ji and Xia.

sentences.zh: 躋字景雲，官至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, office reached Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 夏以貪污棄放於世。

translations.literal: Xia because of corruption was cast aside in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was cast out of public life for corruption.

sentences.zh: 弟智，字子房，貞素有兄風。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, chaste and plain had the elder brother's style.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, was as upright and spare in habit as his brother.

sentences.zh: 少貧窶，每負薪自給，讀誦不輟，竟以儒行稱。

translations.literal: In youth poor and mean, he often carried firewood to supply himself, reading and chanting without ceasing; in the end by Confucian conduct he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in want, often carried firewood to live, and never stopped his studies; in the end he won fame as a Confucian gentleman.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門吏部郎，出為潁川太守。

translations.literal: He successively was Palace Writer Yellow Gates Personnel Ministry gentleman, went out as Yingchuan governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman at the palace secretariat, at the yellow gates, and in the personnel ministry, then became governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 平原管輅嘗謂人曰：「吾與劉潁川兄弟語，使人神思清發，昏不假寐。

translations.literal: Guan Lu of Pingyuan once said to someone, "When I with Liu of Yingchuan and his brothers speak, it causes people's spirit-thought to clear and rise; in dusk I need not borrow sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu of Pingyuan once remarked, "Conversation with Governor Liu of Yingchuan and his brothers clears the mind so that even at dusk I need no nap."

sentences.zh: 自此之外，殆白日欲寢矣。

translations.literal: Outside of this, probably in broad daylight I wish to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: With anyone else I could fall asleep in broad daylight."

sentences.zh: 」入為秘書監，領南陽王師，加散騎常侍，遷侍中、尚書、太常。

translations.literal: " He entered as Director of the Palace Library, concurrently tutor to the Prince of Nanyang, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, transferred Palace Attendant, Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the palace library and tutor to the prince of Nanyang, with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then rose to palace attendant, minister of the secretariat, and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 著《喪服釋疑論》，多所辨明。

translations.literal: He composed Discourse Explaining Doubts on Mourning Dress, much was discriminated and clarified.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Discourse Resolving Doubts on Mourning Garments, which settled many disputed points.

sentences.zh: 太康末卒，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He died at the end of Taikang; his posthumous name was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died toward the end of the Taikang era with the posthumous name Cheng, "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 高光，字宣茂，陳留圉城人，魏太尉柔之子也。

translations.literal: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a man of Yucheng in Chenliu, son of Wei Grand Commandant Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a native of Yucheng in Chenliu, the son of Grand Commandant Gao Rou of Wei.

sentences.zh: 光少習家業，明練刑理。

translations.literal: Guang in youth practiced the family occupation, was clear and practiced in punishments and principles.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he trained in his family's legal tradition and became expert in penal law.

sentences.zh: 初以太子舍人累遷尚書郎，出為幽州刺史、潁州太守。

translations.literal: At first as householder to the heir apparent by accumulated transfers became Secretariat gentleman, went out as Inspector of You Province, governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as household gentleman to the heir apparent and rose to gentleman of the masters of writing, then became inspector of You province and governor of Yingzhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 是時武帝置黃沙獄，以典詔囚。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Wu established Yellow Sand prison, to manage edict prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wu founded the Yellow Sand prison for prisoners sentenced by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 以光曆世明法，用為黃沙御史，秩與中丞同，遷廷尉。

translations.literal: Because Guang through generations understood law, he was used as Yellow Sand censor; rank was the same as the palace assistant secretary; he was promoted Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family had long mastered the code, Guang was named censor of Yellow Sand with rank equal to the palace assistant secretary, then promoted director of justice.

sentences.zh: 元康中，拜尚書，典三公曹。

translations.literal: In Yuankang he was appointed Minister of the Secretariat, in charge of the Three Dukes bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang he was appointed minister of the masters of writing in charge of the Three Dukes section.

sentences.zh: 時趙王倫篡逆，光於其際，守道全貞。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped and rebelled, Guang at that juncture kept the Way and preserved integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun, prince of Zhao, usurped the throne, Guang held to principle and kept his integrity intact.

sentences.zh: 及倫賜死，齊王冏輔政，復以光為廷尉，遷尚書，加奉車都尉。

translations.literal: When Lun was ordered to die, Prince of Qi Jiong assisted governance; again they made Guang Director of Justice, promoted Minister of the Secretariat, added Colonel Who Conducts the Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun was forced to take his life and Prince Jiong of Qi directed the government, Guang was again named director of justice, then minister of the masters of writing with the added title colonel who conducts the carriage.

sentences.zh: 後從駕討成都王穎有勳，封延陵縣公，邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: Later following the carriage in punishing Prince of Chengdu Ying he had merit; he was enfeoffed duke of Yanling county, fief one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the imperial train against Prince Ying of Chengdu and earned distinction; he was enfeoffed as duke of Yanling county with one thousand eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷咸推光明于用法，故頻典理官。

translations.literal: At that time the court all pushed Guang as clear in applying law; therefore repeatedly he managed judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court acknowledged his clarity in applying the law, so he was repeatedly placed over the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 惠帝為張方所逼，幸長安，朝臣奔散，莫有從者，光獨侍帝而西。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui was pressed by Zhang Fang, traveled to Chang'an; court ministers ran and scattered; none had followers; Guang alone attended the emperor going west.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui was driven by Zhang Fang to take refuge in Chang'an and the court fled in panic with none willing to follow, Guang alone accompanied the emperor westward.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted left vice-director of the masters of writing with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 光兄誕為上官巳等所用，曆徐、雍二州刺史。

translations.literal: Guang's elder brother Dan was used by Shangguan Si and others, successively was Inspector of Xu and Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's elder brother Dan was employed by Shangguan Si and his faction and served as inspector of Xu and Yong provinces in turn.

sentences.zh: 誕性任放無倫次，而決烈過人，與光異操。

translations.literal: Dan's nature was unbridled and unrestrained without order, yet decisive and fierce surpassing others; with Guang his conduct differed.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was wild and unmethodical, yet bolder than most—a temper quite unlike his brother's.

sentences.zh: 常謂光小節，恆輕侮之，光事誕愈謹。

translations.literal: He always called Guang petty scruples, constantly treated him lightly and insulted him; Guang serving Dan became more careful.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly mocked Guang for fussiness and treated him with contempt, yet Guang served his elder brother with growing deference.

sentences.zh: 帝既還洛陽，時太弟新立，重選傅訓，以光為少傅，加光祿大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor had returned to Luoyang, at the time the imperial younger brother was newly established; heavily selecting tutors and instruction, they made Guang Junior Tutor, added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, the heir-designate had just been installed and tutors were chosen with care; Guang was named junior tutor with the added title grand master of splendid carriage while keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝即位，加光祿大夫金章紫綬，與傅祗並見推崇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, he added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage gold seal purple ribbon, together with Fu Zhi both were seen honored and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai came to the throne, Guang received the grand master of splendid carriage's gold seal and purple ribbon and was honored together with Fu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書令，本官如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he became Director of the Masters of Writing; original offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named director of the masters of writing while retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，贈司空、侍中。

translations.literal: Because of illness he died; posthumously Minister of Works, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously named minister of works and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 屬京洛傾覆，竟未加諡。

translations.literal: It fell when capital and Luoyang overturned; in the end no posthumous name was added.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Luoyang followed so closely that no posthumous title was ever conferred.

sentences.zh: 子韜字子遠，放佚無檢。

translations.literal: His son Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was dissolute and unrestrained without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was dissolute and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 光為廷尉時，韜受貨賕，有司奏案之，而光不知。

translations.literal: When Guang was Director of Justice, Tao received goods and bribes; the responsible office memorialized to investigate him, yet Guang did not know.
translations.idiomatic: While Guang served as director of justice, Tao took bribes; the authorities impeached him, yet Guang knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 時人雖非光不能防閑其子，以其用心有素，不以為累。

translations.literal: Men of the time although blamed Guang for not being able to guard and restrain his son, because his using heart had long been plain, they did not regard it as a burden.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries faulted him for failing to restrain his son, yet because his own integrity was long established they did not let the scandal touch his reputation.

sentences.zh: 初，光詣長安留台，以韜兼右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guang went to Chang'an's remaining terrace, he made Tao concurrently General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Guang went to the provisional administration at Chang'an, he had Tao act concurrently as general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 韜與殿省小人交通，及光卒，仍於喪中往來不絕。

translations.literal: Tao trafficked with petty men of the palace halls and secretariat; when Guang died, still in mourning he went and came without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had dealings with low palace clerks, and after Guang's death he kept up those visits even during mourning.

sentences.zh: 時東海王越輔政，不朝觀。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of the Eastern Sea Yue assisted governance, did not attend court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue of the Eastern Sea then directed the government and no longer attended court.

sentences.zh: 韜知人心有望，密與太傅參軍薑賾、京兆杜概等謀討越，事泄伏誅。

translations.literal: Tao knew men's hearts had expectation; secretly with Grand Tutor aide Jiang Ze, Jingzhao Du Gai, and others plotted to punish Yue; the affair leaked and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sensed growing resentment against Yue and secretly plotted with the grand tutor's aide Jiang Ze, Du Gai of Jingzhao, and others to strike at him; the plot leaked and Tao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：下士競而文，中庸靜而質，不若進不足而退有餘也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lower gentlemen strive and are ornate; the middle way is quiet and plain; not as good as advancing insufficient yet retreating having surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Petty men strive for outward polish and the middling keep a dull quiet—both fall short of advancing with restraint and withdrawing while still leaving something in hand.

sentences.zh: 魏舒、劉寔發慮精華，結綬登槐，覽止成務。

translations.literal: Wei Shu and Liu Shi emitted thought's essence, tied ribbons and ascended the locust, viewed stop and completed tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu and Liu Shi brought the finest of their judgment to bear, took high office beneath the court locusts, and saw their policies through to completion.

sentences.zh: 季和切問近對，當官正色。

translations.literal: Jihe cut questions and near answers; holding office with correct color.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi of courtesy Jihe answered sharp questions with plain good sense and kept a straight face in office.

sentences.zh: 詩云「貪人敗類」，豈劉夏之謂歟！

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'Greedy men ruin the kind' — how could it mean Liu Xia!
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, "Greedy men destroy their kin"—can that mean anyone but Liu Xia?"

sentences.zh: 贊曰：舒言不矜，憙對千乘。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Shu's words were not boastful; Xi faced a thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Shu spoke without swagger; Xi faced princes of a thousand chariots undaunted.

sentences.zh: 子真、宣茂，雅志難陵。

translations.literal: Zizhen, Xuanmao — lofty aims hard to violate.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen and Xuanmao—noble purpose none could overthrow.

sentences.zh: 進忠能舉，退讓攸興。

translations.literal: Advancing loyalty, able to raise; withdrawing yielding, thereby rising.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed loyalty and lifted the worthy; in yielding office they set a lasting example.

sentences.zh: 皎皎瑚器，來光玉繩。

translations.literal: Bright bright coral vessel; coming light to jade cord.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as ritual coral, they brought luster to the constellations of state.
